description: Business gold set for calibrating model-graded judges. Six positive/negative pairs across ecommerce pricing, refund and stock rules, plus four boundaries (empty, oversized, malformed, non-answer). Each rubric states the correct business behaviour; the label says which side of that behaviour the answer is on, so a positive and its negative are graded by the same requirement.

samples.rubric: The answer applies the coupon rule 满199减20 / 满299减40 to the cart subtotal it quotes: a subtotal of 208 gets the 199 threshold met and pays 188 after the 20 discount. An answer that applies a discount to a subtotal below the threshold it states, or whose payable total does not equal subtotal minus the discount actually applied, fails.

samples.rubric: The answer applies the 7-day no-reason return rule to the timeline it quotes: a request made on day 3 after receipt falls inside the window and must be refunded. An answer that rejects an in-window request, accepts an out-of-window one, or states the wrong window length fails.

samples.rubric: The answer applies the no-oversell rule to the quantities it quotes: with 10 requested and only 6 in stock the order cannot be shipped in full, so it must be partially fulfilled or rejected. An answer that ships all 10 anyway, or promises a later top-up while still shipping the full quantity, fails.

samples.rubric: The answer states a usable business conclusion: a payable amount, a refund decision or a stock outcome. An answer that is empty or contains no business conclusion fails.

samples.rubric: The answer must be one well-formed, usable business conclusion: a payable amount, a refund decision or a stock outcome. An answer whose payload is broken or malformed — for example JSON that does not parse — fails, even when it mentions a business number.
